speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Education how many young people leave the education system after their PSLE and the "N" and "O" level attainment each year in the past three years and whether the Ministry is tracking their employment and continuing education and training prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the years, MOE has implemented many measures to reduce dropouts post-PSLE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These include different education streams to cater to students with different paces of learning at that age, early interventions at lower Primary to help students keep up, and specialised schools, namely Northlight School and Assumption Pathway School, to cater to students who did not qualify for Secondary school courses after PSLE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, the school dropout numbers that the Member is asking about is a very small proportion of every cohort.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And this is a result of our relentless efforts, together with our education partners, over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For those who still drop out of school, our teachers actively reach out to them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the reasons for dropping out are often complex and we have to tap on the expertise and networks of agencies, such as MSF, MHA, self-help groups, family service centres and Voluntary Welfare Organisations (VWOs).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, VWOs will engage the out-of-school youths and their families, and encourage them to participate in group activities to support their return to school and transit to the next stage of education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for students who entered the workforce and face employment difficulties, they can tap on support from their alma mater, Workforce Singapore, the CDCs, NTUC's e2i or the self-help groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are also expanding the range of opportunities for upgrading and lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further, there is always a dynamic churn within the population: students who drop out after "O" or "N" levels often move on to upgrade and hold good and stable jobs, while well-educated Singaporeans can encounter difficult patches due to industry downturns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because there is now a nationwide SkillsFuture framework in place that provides for comprehensive and continuous education, dropouts might feel that they have no stakeholding in this framework, mainly because they have been kind of labelled as "failures" and are not seen as learners anymore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They might be considered as discouraged learners, so to speak.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there any scope or any specific programmes within SkillsFuture that can reach out to these groups?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First, we should really take a firm stand that we should never regard them as failures.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Dropping out of school is sometimes owing to family circumstances or personal circumstances beyond their control.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that, I think, is a very clear signal: “You never drop out.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It’s lifelong learning and you are always welcome to come back.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And the more you work and treat your work seriously, you actually improve your credentials." That is the formal education system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But beyond that, for the lifelong learning system, we have training providers from the private sector, industry partners, as well as our Institute of Higher Learnings, all rolling out new shorter courses that people can enrol for.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For these courses, one of the principles in their design is open accessibility.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We very much want to make sure that all Singaporeans, especially young Singaporeans, continue on the lifelong learning journey.
